steps.text: If you will use Insteon software, write down the Load Controller's Insteon ID and the location of the appliance it will control.
At the circuit breaker or fuse panel, turn off the circuit supplying the junction box wired to the appliance you want to control.
Remove the junction box cover and disconnect the two supply lines coming from the circuit breaker, leaving 1/2 inch of bare, clean copper wire on the ends.

Connect the Load Controller to the load and the junction box as shown in the wiring diagram; its wires are Line 1, Line 2, Load and Load. The ground wire is not connected to the Load Controller; cap it with a wire nut.
Make sure all wire connectors are firmly attached and no copper is exposed except the ground wire.
Turn the circuit back on at the circuit breaker or fuse panel.
Test the Load Controller: press the SET button to turn the load on.
Press the SET button again to turn the load off.

notes: The Load Controller must be connected through a 2-pole tandem circuit breaker rated for no more than 30 amps, as it has no over-current protection.
It does not require a neutral connection. Use only copper or copper-clad wire.
Installation by a qualified electrician is recommended.
The 240V Load Controller 2477SA Owner's Manual lists tools to mount the Load Controller to a wall but gives no mounting steps.

steps.text: At each responder, set it to the state you want the Load Controller to activate. If the responder is a multi-scene device, tap the scene button you want to control until its LED turns on.
Press and hold the SET button until the Load Controller beeps (3 seconds).
Press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Load Controller double-beeps and its status LED turns solid green if the load is on, or solid red if it is off

notes: The device that goes into linking mode first becomes the controller. For most controllers, press and hold an On or scene button for 10 seconds or the SET button for 3 seconds.
Linking mode times out after 4 minutes.
To link several responders, repeat the controller steps for each one.

steps.text: Use the SET button to set the load to the state you want.
Put the controller in linking mode: for most controllers, press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the Load Controller's SET button until it double-beeps (3 seconds).
steps.expect: Status LED flashes once, then turns solid green if the load is on, or solid red if it is off

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button until the Load Controller beeps (3 seconds).
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1: as an extended message if Get Insteon Engine Version (cmd1 0x0D) says the device is i2CS, and as a standard message otherwise.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, and the device's group 1 to the Hub as a controller, so the Hub receives the device's reports.

To add the device without its SET button, have the Hub send it Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09, cmd2 0x01; extended for an i2CS device) right after it starts ALL-Linking, in place of the SET button step.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request, Enter Linking Mode and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: If the responder is a multi-scene device, tap the scene button to remove until its LED turns on.
Press and hold the SET button until the Load Controller beeps (3 seconds).
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps (3 seconds).
Within 4 minutes, press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Load Controller double-beeps and its status LED turns solid green or red to show the load state

steps.text: Put the controller in unlinking mode: for most controllers, press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the controller's SET button for 3 seconds again.
Press and hold the Load Controller's SET button until it double-beeps (3 seconds).
steps.expect: Status LED flashes once, then turns solid green if the load is on, or solid red if it is off

notes: For most controllers, unlinking mode is entered by pressing and holding an On or scene button for 10 seconds twice, or the SET button for 3 seconds twice.

steps.text: Unlink the Load Controller from any controllers, and unlink any responders it controls.
At the circuit breaker or fuse panel, turn off the circuit supplying the junction box.
Wait about 10 seconds.
While holding down the SET button, turn the circuit back on, making sure not to let go of the SET button.
Continue to hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: A few seconds later the Load Controller double-beeps, its status LED turns solid green and the load turns on

notes: Depending on where the breaker panel is, you may need a helper.

steps.text: Unlink the Load Controller from every controller linked to it; otherwise the controllers retry their commands and slow down the system.
Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub send Enter Unlinking Mode (cmd1 0x0A) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Have the Hub send Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09) with cmd2 0x01, for group 1, as an extended message if the device is i2CS.
Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from the standard Insteon commands Enter Unlinking Mode, Start ALL-Linking and Enter Linking Mode; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.
